quote: The commensal microbiota and complement were both required for P. gingivalis-induced bone loss, as germ-free mice or conventionally raised C3a and C5a receptor-deficient mice did not develop bone loss after inoculation with P. gingivalis.
summary: Mice deficient in C3a and C5a receptors did not develop P. gingivalis-induced inflammatory periodontal bone loss, implying receptor signalling drives disease (periodontitis, not UC).

quote: It acts as a friend in the defense against pathogens, by inducing opsonization and a direct killing by C5b-9 membrane attack complex and by triggering inflammatory responses with the anaphylatoxins C3a and C5a.
summary: General review of complement in immunity and disease that discusses C5a signalling without new data on the C5a receptor or on UC.

quote: NLRP3 assembly requires intracellular C5 activation and stimulation of C5a receptor 1 (C5aR1), which is negatively regulated by surface-expressed C5aR2.
summary: C5aR1 stimulation is required for NLRP3 inflammasome assembly in human CD4+ T cells, driving IL-1beta, IFN-gamma and Th1 differentiation.

quote: Here we demonstrate that IgG1 immune complexes (ICs), the inhibitory IgG receptor FcγRIIB and the C-type lectin–like receptor dectin-1 suppress C5a receptor (C5aR) functions.
summary: Galactosylated IgG1 immune complexes suppress C5aR signalling and C5a-dependent inflammation in vitro and in vivo; C5aR itself was not directly perturbed and UC was not studied.

quote: This mechanism to disengage bacterial clearance from inflammation required an intimate crosstalk between TLR2 and the complement receptor C5aR and can contribute to the persistence of microbial communities that drive dysbiotic diseases.
summary: P. gingivalis exploits C5aR crosstalk with TLR2 in neutrophils to uncouple bacterial clearance from inflammation, promoting dysbiotic inflammation in periodontitis.

quote: This review will highlight major developments in C5a receptor research that support C5aR as an important therapeutic target.
summary: Review of C5a receptor function, structure and antagonists, presenting C5aR as a therapeutic target without new data.
Paper concerns MSC therapy in sepsis and only measures C5a ligand levels in blood, not the C5a receptor.
Paper concerns necroptosis, NETs and complement in ANCA vasculitis; C5a is mentioned only in passing, not the receptor.
Paper concerns tissue factor in antiphospholipid fetal injury; C5a is the ligand and the receptor is not examined.

quote: Genetic and pharmacological blockade of C3aR/C5aR signal transduction in nT reg cells augments in vitro and in vivo suppression, abrogates autoimmune colitis, and prolongs allogeneic skin graft survival.
summary: Blocking C3aR/C5aR signalling in natural regulatory T cells enhances their suppressive function and abrogates autoimmune colitis in mice, so receptor signalling worsens colitis.
Review of myeloid-derived suppressor cells that lists C5a as an inducer of differentiation, not the receptor.

quote: Complement-activating properties of anti-FcepsilonRIalpha autoAbs can indeed be of pathogenetic relevance, because C5a receptor blockade on basophils as well as decomplementation reduced drastically the histamine-releasing capacity of most anti-FcepsilonRIalpha-reactive CU sera.
summary: C5a receptor blockade on basophils sharply reduced histamine release induced by urticaria patient sera, a non-UC setting.

quote: We found that neutrophils released cellular adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in response to exogenous stimuli such as formylated bacterial peptides and inflammatory mediators that activated Fcgamma, interleukin-8, C5a complement, and leukotriene B(4) receptors.
summary: C5a receptor is only one of several stimulus receptors listed as triggering neutrophil ATP release; no result specific to it.
Paper concerns CD55 deficiency (CHAPLE syndrome); C5a is only a downstream readout and the receptor is not studied.
General complement review that mentions the C5a ligand, with no content on the C5a receptor gene.
Paper concerns iRHOM2/TACE in arthritis; C5a is only a stimulus and the receptor is not examined.
Paper shows the C5a ligand promotes IL-22 and IL-17 in T cells in macular degeneration; the receptor is not studied.
Paper concerns bFGF and leukocyte recruitment; C5a is only an inflammatory stimulus and the receptor is not studied.
Paper concerns the leukotriene B4 receptor knockout; C5a appears only as a control stimulus.
Old study of complement-derived chemotactic factors (C5a ligand) in synovial fluid; the receptor is not studied.

quote: We also show that a substantial proportion of intestinal macrophages express chemokine receptors for interleukin (IL)-8 and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-beta), and a smaller proportion expresses receptors for N-formylmethionyl-leucyl-phenylalanine and C5a, but, surprisingly, they do not migrate to the corresponding ligands.
summary: A smaller proportion of human intestinal macrophages express the C5a receptor, yet they do not migrate to C5a, unlike blood monocytes.

quote: C5a exerts a pro-inflammatory effect via the G-protein-coupled receptor C5a anaphylatoxin chemotactic receptor 1 (C5aR1, also known as CD88) that is expressed on cells of myeloid origin.
summary: Structural study of C5aR1 bound to the antagonist NDT9513727 showing an extra-helical binding mode; no inflammation or colitis outcome measured.
Paper shows granzyme K activates complement, generating C5a; the C5a receptor is not studied.

quote: Moreover, microbial hijacking of C5aR (CD88) signaling in neutrophils impairs their antimicrobial function while promoting destructive inflammatory responses.
summary: Review of neutrophil homeostasis in periodontitis noting that microbial hijacking of C5aR signalling promotes destructive inflammation; no UC data.

quote: We identified new associations at CCR1, STAT4 and KLRC4.
summary: GWAS in Behcet's disease identified a new susceptibility locus at CCR1 with an expression-associated variant; IBD is mentioned only for IL23R and IL10.
